messages:
Alex P.: Quick question — noticed a handful of traces in staging where spans inside the same trace are attributed to different tenant ids (edge proxy sets x-tenant header). How should we route/export these? Slice traces per-tenant, or export whole trace and tag spans? Thinking about retention, RBAC, and billing.
Mira S.: Ugh, been expecting this. Two main schools: 1) trace-slicing at collector (create N traces, one per tenant) — clean per-tenant datasets but you lose global trace continuity. 2) per-span export (keep one trace id but spans live in different tenant datasets) — keeps continuity but complicates RBAC/retention and may expose spans across tenants in the storage layer.
Tim R.: FWIW my leaning is collector-side slicing with explicit "owned_by" attribute on each new root span so we can still link slices for debugging without mixing storage. Example sketch:
```python
# pseudo-collector handler
tenant = span.resource.attributes.get('tenant.id') or span.attributes.get('http.request.headers.x-tenant')
if tenant:
    new_root = clone_span_with_new_trace_id(span, resource={"tenant.id": tenant})
    exporter.route(tenant, new_root)
else:
    exporter.route(default, span)
```
Problems: sampling decisions need to be consistent, and reassembling cross-tenant traces in the Console must be explicit.
Sasha K.: Two concerns: (1) legal/PII — if a span contains customer-identifying metadata but is routed to wrong tenant we'd have an issue. (2) UX for SREs — if we slice traces, debugging multi-tenant flow (e.g., proxy -> backend -> db) is harder. We should provide a "stitch" metadata token so Console can show related slices but only to allowed users.
Jordan L.: Billing/quotas note: if we slice, do we charge each tenant for the spans they "own" only? Edge-case: shared infrastructure spans (proxy) — which tenant pays? We should define ownership rules: incoming request header -> owner, else proxy as infra tenant (bill to infra or platform). Avoid double-counting.
Elaine (PM): From product side: requirement = strict per-tenant retention & RBAC. We must be able to expire tenant A's data without touching tenant B. Also need an observable way to show when a trace was sliced and which slices correspond. Propose a small RFC + spike: "collector: tenant-slicing spec" with config knobs: fallback_owner, stitch_token, retention_label.
Mira S.: Implementation notes: do this at the otel-collector layer (processor). Add a "tenant-router" processor that emits per-tenant traces and injects metadata: "redwood.slice.id" and "redwood.slice.stitch_token". Exporters already support tenancy headers so route by tenant to exporter(s).
Tim R.: Also watch sampling — if original trace was sampled=0 but slice needs sampling for tenant debugging, we might need local re-sampling; need guardrails to avoid increasing global egress.
Sasha K.: Security idea: only allow stitch_token to be visible to principals with "telemetry:stitch" RBAC. Default console view hides cross-tenant links unless you have permission. That satisfies compliance teams.
Alex P.: Operationally, what about exporter backpressure? If tenant-specific exporter is down, fallback should be: 1) queue to shared cold-storage (encrypted) OR 2) send to per-customer dead-letter with retention policy = platform defaults. Which is preferred?
Jordan L.: For billing transparency, prefer dead-letter that is tagged with tenant and billed at cheaper rate but causes alert if exporter down for >5m. Make sure quotas prevent one noisy tenant from overflowing shared fallback.
infra-bot: otel-collector: tenant-router v0.3 started, routing table loaded (tenants: 42), dark-launch mode ON
Mira S.: I'll add unit tests for span ownership extraction heuristics and a small e2e with the collector in front of a fake exporter. Tim — want you to do a perf spike for cloning traces at 10k tps.
Tim R.: Happy to spike. I'll measure CPU/memory overhead and bandwidth when we clone vs tag-only. Plan: three runs (no-slice, tag-only, slice) and post numbers.
Elaine (PM): Action items: Alex open RFC + design doc, Tim spike perf, Mira tests + processor PR, Sasha to mock Console "stitch" UX and RBAC flows, Jordan to write billing rules draft. Target: RFC + spike in 2w.
Alex P.: Sounds good. I'll create the RFC now: <https://redwood-internal/rfc/tenant-slicing> — please add comments. :thumbsup:
Mira S.: +1. I'll drop a sample collector config in the RFC.
Sasha K.: I'll sketch the console wireframes in figma and link.
Jordan L.: I'll add quota rules doc under billing repo.
Alex P.: Thanks all. If anyone sees a counterexample (e.g., spans from multiple tenants that truly must remain in one trace for correctness), ping here and let's escalate.
Elaine (PM): Thanks — marking as "sync" for next infra sync meeting.
